mathematical_sources.note: Theorem 2, printed page 2, and proof on printed page 9. The source convention countable means countably infinite; our explicit Nonempty, Countable, metrizable and perfect hypotheses give the same scope. PDF directly consulted; SHA256 cd7a764d023a930c4792545378732856fb73c76e2a9abe74a03cdd235ee28108. The formal proof uses scheduled binary clopen splits rather than the source closure/Cantor-group translation route. Sierpiński 1920 and Dasgupta 2005 are historical references cited by Francis; their originals were not independently consulted.
mathematical_sources.title: Two Topological Uniqueness Theorems for Spaces of Real Numbers, arXiv:1210.1008v1

related_formalizations.note: Uses upstream countable completely-regular clopen-basis theorem, binary prefix API, lexicographic orders, countable dense-order isomorphism and the existing real-induced rational topology. The general topology-to-compatible-order construction is proved here.

Apache-2.0 clopen splitting, enumeration and binary address infrastructure adapted with attribution. New finite-protected splits, three-stage schedule, two-sided addresses and topology equality are proved here. No local cross-project imports or prior-registration assumptions.
